A.explanation: Too small by a factor of about 1000. It results from a prefix error when converting $2.09 \times 10^{-8}$ to $\text{V m}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: About one quarter of the required value. It results from using the electron mass instead of the larger proton mass.

C.explanation: About one half of the required value. It results from using $1.00 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ instead of $2.00 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ for the acceleration.

D.explanation: Combines $F = ma$ for the proton with $E = F/q$ to give $E \approx 2.09 \times 10^{-8} \text{ V m}^{-1} = 20.9 \text{ nV m}^{-1}$.

hints: Notice the proton has acceleration $2.00 \text{ m s}^{-2}$, so first find the electric force on it from $F = ma$ using proton mass $1.67 \times 10^{-27} \text{ kg}$.
Connect that force to field strength with $E = F/q$, where the proton charge is $1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and $E$ is in $\text{V m}^{-1}$.
Calculate $ma/q$ and convert the $10^{-8} \text{ V m}^{-1}$ result into $\text{nV m}^{-1}$ using $1 \text{ nV} = 10^{-9} \text{ V}$.
walkthrough: Identify the given motion: a proton of mass $m = 1.67 \times 10^{-27} \text{ kg}$ and charge $q = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ accelerates at $a = 2.00 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
State the governing physics: the field exerts force $F = ma$, and electric field strength is defined by $E = F/q$, so $E = ma/q$.
Substitute values with units: $E = (1.67 \times 10^{-27} \text{ kg})(2.00 \text{ m s}^{-2})/(1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C})$.
Calculate the numerator: $F = 3.34 \times 10^{-27} \text{ N}$, then $E = 3.34 \times 10^{-27}/1.60 \times 10^{-19} = 2.09 \times 10^{-8} \text{ N C}^{-1} = 2.09 \times 10^{-8} \text{ V m}^{-1}$.
Check units and prefix: $10^{-9} \text{ V m}^{-1} = 1 \text{ nV m}^{-1}$, so $2.09 \times 10^{-8} \text{ V m}^{-1} = 20.9 \text{ nV m}^{-1}$. This is option D.
